title: 'Synth Lead' is clipping
detail: Sample peaks reach +0.8 dBFS. Anything at or above 0 dBFS distorts on export and in any fixed-point stage.
steps: Lower the clip gain or input trim of 'Synth Lead' by 1.8 dB, before any plugins.
If the peaks come from a plugin in the chain, lower that plugin's output instead.
Re-check the peak meter: it should now stay below -1 dBFS.

title: 'Pad' is out of phase between left and right
detail: Phase correlation is -1.00. In mono the two sides cancel and the track drops in level or vanishes.
steps: Put 'Pad' in mono and compare the level to stereo.
If it is a stereo-miked or DI+amp source, invert the polarity of one side only.
If it comes from a widener or chorus, reduce the width/amount until correlation stays above 0.

title: Low-end build-up on 'Lead Vox'
detail: 75% of its energy sits below 120 Hz, where it competes with kick and bass without adding anything you hear in the mix.
steps: Add a high-pass filter on 'Lead Vox' at 100 Hz, 12 or 18 dB/oct.
Sweep it up while playing the full mix until the track starts to sound thin, then back off by a third.
Compare the kick and bass clarity with the filter bypassed.

title: 'Bass' and 'Kick' mask each other around 45 Hz
detail: 80% spectral overlap; the strongest clash is the 20 Hz-100 Hz band, where the levels differ by only 1.3 dB.
steps: Insert an EQ on 'Bass' (it has the lower priority here).
Add a bell at 45 Hz, Q 0.6, and cut 4.0 dB.
Play both tracks together: 'Kick' should come forward without 'Bass' sounding thin.
If 'Bass' loses body, use a dynamic EQ band side-chained from 'Kick' instead of a static cut.

title: 'Keys' and 'Guitar' mask each other around 245 Hz
detail: 80% spectral overlap; the strongest clash is the 200 Hz-300 Hz band, where the levels differ by only 2.0 dB.
steps: Insert an EQ on 'Keys' (it has the lower priority here).
Add a bell at 245 Hz, Q 2.4, and cut 4.0 dB.
Play both tracks together: 'Guitar' should come forward without 'Keys' sounding thin.
If 'Keys' loses body, use a dynamic EQ band side-chained from 'Guitar' instead of a static cut.

title: 'OH' and 'Room' are 0.77 ms out of time
detail: They share the same source (correlation +0.66) but 'Room' arrives 37.0 samples later, which comb-filters the sum.
steps: Add a sample-delay plugin on 'OH' and delay it by 37.0 samples (0.77 ms).
Alternatively nudge the 'Room' audio 0.77 ms earlier on the timeline.
Play both together: the low end should get fuller, not thinner.

title: Stereo low end on 'Bass'
detail: 80% of the energy is below 150 Hz and the side channel is only -0.2 dB under the mid. Low frequencies in the sides waste headroom and fold unpredictably to mono.
steps: Insert a mid/side EQ or bass-mono utility on 'Bass'.
Make everything below 120 Hz mono (or high-pass the side channel at 120 Hz).
Check that the track keeps its width above that frequency.

title: 'Synth Lead' is harsh around 2.5 kHz
detail: This region is 16.0 dB above the track's own spectral tilt; the ear is most sensitive here, so it reads as fatiguing.
steps: Insert a bell (or dynamic EQ) band on 'Synth Lead' at 2.5 kHz, Q 4.0.
Cut 6.0 dB; with a dynamic EQ set it to act only on the loud notes.
A/B at matched loudness: the track should sound smoother, not duller.

title: Mix is louder than the loudness target
detail: Integrated loudness is -10.6 LUFS; the target is -14.0 LUFS. Streaming services will turn it down by 3.4 dB.
steps: Reduce the limiter input on the mix bus by about 3.4 dB.
Louder than target only costs dynamics once the platform normalises it.

title: Pan 'Guitar' and 'Keys' apart
detail: Both are effectively mono and centred, and 80% of their spectra overlap. Spatial separation unmasks them without EQ.
steps: Pan 'Guitar' to about L 30.
Pan 'Keys' to about R 30.
Check the balance in mono afterwards: both should still be audible.
